messages:
anna kim: Heads-up — product asked for privacy-aware tenant views for the new customer dashboards. Need to lock down what runtime/infra metrics we expose per-tenant (and how we mask/pseudonymize).

mike rao: +1. Do we have a proposed data contract from runtime side? what fields are safe to surface? :thinking_face: 

sarah liu: From infra: we can provide aggregated QPS, p50/p95/p99 latency, active sessions, and recent error-rate. We can also emit 'noisy_neighbor_score' optionally. Raw request ids or prompt text are blocked by default.

anna kim: Good. Two asks from product: 1) per-tenant metrics in console (customer-facing) 2) internal per-org admin view with more detailed signals for SRE. These need different masking levels.

josh taylor: For masking, suggest levels: public (customer console) = aggregated per-5m, no identifiers, RLS applied; internal = per-tenant flow with hashed ids and 30d retention; debug = full (on-demand, audited). We need RBAC plumbing in Console to enforce.

mike rao: Runtime needs to tag metrics with tenant_id in telemetry layer. We can emit two streams: metrics_public and metrics_internal. Public stream will drop tenant_id and only include 'tenant_alias' that product controls. Internal stream contains hashed_tenant_id. Both streams should include these fields: ["time_bucket","metric","value","quantile","source_host","model_variant","route_tag"].

anna kim: Can you paste an example ingest query for the public stream? product wants to understand rollup windows & sample rates.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline v2 to metrics-ingest completed at 1777778900 — public/internal streams enabled.

mike rao: Example (pseudo SQL):
```
SELECT time_bucket('5m', ts) AS tb, metric, approx_percentile(value, 0.95) AS p95, SUM(count) AS total
FROM metrics_public
WHERE metric IN ('token_qps','latency_ms','error_rate')
GROUP BY tb, metric
ORDER BY tb
```
Notes: public stream uses 5m buckets and 99% sampling on raw events to reduce PII risk.

sarah liu: Noisy neighbor detection signals we can provide: 1) delta_qps (tenant vs baseline), 2) growing batch_wait_time, 3) accelerated cache_misses, 4) KV-cache-evictions-per-tenant. We can expose a composite noisy_neighbor_score computed in runtime (0-100).

josh taylor: Important: composite score should be deterministic and include weighting config. Where do we surface config? Console-team?

console-team: We'll need an API to fetch weighting config and to display contributing signals in the UI. Also need to show recommended mitigations (throttle, reroute, contact CSM). UX suggests an expand/collapse explanation per signal.

eva: Data-privacy note: any per-tenant telemetry that could be traced to an end-user must be redacted. We need a privacy review on the internal stream schema before rollout. ETA for review?

anna kim: Let's do privacy review in parallel. Plan: 1) runtime to publish schema PR to infra repo by EOD Wed (mike) 2) infra to enable hashed_tenant_ids and noisy score in internal stream (sarah) 3) console-team to build a privacy-aware rendering component and RBAC gates (console-team) 4) product to provision sample tenant_alias mapping (anna)

mike rao: I'll open the PR. Will include example ingestion queries and cost estimate for extra metrics (mostly small).

sarah liu: I can flip noisy score on in staging by tomorrow. Will also add retention flag for internal stream (30d default).

josh taylor: Ops: add a rollout gate — start with 5 enterprise customers (opt-in), monitor false positives on noisy score for 2 weeks, then ramp.

anna kim: Sounds good. @eva can you schedule privacy review for Thursday?

eva: Scheduling now. Also adding checklist: data minimization, retention, access logs, and KMS key use for hashed ids.

console-team: We'll prototpye a dashboard card that shows p95 latency, token_qps, noisy_score and the top 3 contributing signals. Will attach mock by Fri.

mike rao: FYI — need to confirm cost impact for metrics_public retention beyond 90d. If product wants historical trends >90d that might go to cheaper cold storage with rollup.

anna kim: Document decisions in the product runbook. We'll reconvene next Tue after PR + staging flip. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
